source.title: isBetween() with date-only string bounds drops the written day in non-UTC workflow timezones

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

In a workflow expression, `DateTime.local(2023, 6, 16, 23, 0).isBetween('2023-06-16', '2023-06-17')` returns `false` when the workflow timezone is west of UTC (for example America/New_York), even though 23:00 on June 16 is inside the written range. Date-only string bounds go through `new Date()`, which parses them as UTC midnight; converted into the workflow timezone, `'2023-06-16'` becomes June 15, 8:00 PM in New York. East of UTC the bounds land mid-day instead of midnight. The same shift affects partial date-only strings (`'2023-06'`, `'2023'`).

I reproduced this in n8n's own expression test suites (`packages/workflow` and `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime`): a regression test with the expression above fails on current master in the default America/New_York test timezone.

### To Reproduce

1. Set a workflow's timezone to America/New_York (workflow Settings).
2. Evaluate `{{ DateTime.local(2023, 6, 16, 23, 0).isBetween('2023-06-16', '2023-06-17') }}` in an expression, for example in a Set node.
3. The result is `false`.

### Expected behavior

`true`. Date-only string bounds should mean midnight in the workflow timezone, the same way `.toDateTime()` already parses `'2023-06-16'` (`tryToParseDateTime` uses `DateTime.fromISO`, i.e. local midnight).

### Debug Info

Reproduced on current master (2.45.0) through the test suites above (Node 24). I did not run a separate UI test; the steps above are the reproduction path for the same code. Related: #42064 reports the same class of bug for String.toDate - this is a different code path (isBetween bounds via convertToDateTime), not covered by its PR #42065.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux 22.04

### n8n Version

2.45.0 (current master, source)

### Node.js Version

24.18.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted
